title: Local, bring-your-own-AI sprite pipeline with pixelization and sprite sheet export
author: krzysztof_radomski
selftext:
For a while I'd been generating game assets locally with different AI tools, comparing, making a mess, regenerating etc etc. Maybe there was a away that was more hmm streamlined. In know there are tools, but I wanted my own. That thing eventually turned into Spritewright: [https://github.com/krzysztofradomski/spritewright](https://github.com/krzysztofradomski/spritewright)

It runs entirely on your machine and works with whatever it can detect on your system, whether that's a Claude or Codex subscription, Gemini or OpenAI API keys, or a local ComfyUI, so you don't need another subscription just to make sprites. 

You write a prompt, it generates candidates, and you decide what gets approved. Along the way it can turn images into proper pixel art that all share one palette, so a set of sprites actually looks like it belongs to the same game, and it exports sprite sheets with atlases when you're done.  
What still sucks is the animation. I tried again and again to build a decent pipeline for it, but I couldn't get frames consistent enough to be usable, sso right now that part is what I experiment with in Godot using available system nodes like the bone spring animation thing.

Anyway, maybe some of you will find it useful.
